records.label: spacr.ome_zarr#11
records.source: **2. Units are translated through an explicit table, and an unknown one is refused.** :data:`NGFF_UNIT_TO_SPACR` is the mapping, written out. A unit that is not in it raises :class:`OmeZarrError`. It would be one line to default to ``"px"`` instead, and that one line is how a 0.65 µm pixel becomes a 0.65 px pixel and every downstream area comes out wrong by a factor of 10^6 — in a column named ``cell_area`` that still looks entirely reasonable. The error distinguishes the two cases that need different fixes: a unit NGFF has never heard of (the file is wrong), and a legal NGFF unit spaCR has no short token for (convert it, e.g. to ``micrometer``).
records.context: **2. Units are translated through an explicit table, and an unknown one is refused.** :data:`NGFF_UNIT_TO_SPACR` is the mapping, written out. A unit that is not in it throws :class:`OmeZarrError`. It would be one line to default to ``"px"`` instead, and that one line is how a 0.65 µm pixel becomes a 0.65 px pixel and every downstream area comes out wrong by a factor of 10^6 — in a column named ``cell_area`` that still looks entirely reasonable. The error distinguishes the two cases that need different fixes: a unit NGFF has never heard of (the file is wrong), and a legal NGFF unit spaCR has no short token for (convert it, e.g. to ``micrometer``).
records.translation: **2. Enheter översätts genom en explicit tabell, och en okänd vägras.** :data:`NGFF_UNIT_TO_SPACR` är mappningen, skriven ut. En enhet som inte är i den kastar :class:`OmeZarrError`. Det skulle vara en linje till standard till ``"px"`` i stället, och att en rad är hur en 0,65 µm pixel blir en 2,6 px pixel och varje nedströms område kommer ut fel med en faktor på 10 ^ 6 — i en kolumn som heter ``cell_area`` som fortfarande ser helt rimligt. Felet skiljer mellan två fall som behöver olika rättningar: en enhet som NGFF aldrig har hört talas om (filen är fel), och en laglig NGFF-enhet spaCR som inte har någon kort symbol för (konvertera den, till exempel till ``micrometer``).

records.label: spacr.ome_zarr#15
records.source: **0.4 is implemented properly** — it is what essentially all real data is in, and it is zarr-format 2. 0.5 (zarr-format 3, metadata under an ``ome`` key in ``zarr.json``) is *tolerated*: its metadata is parsed in full, and its chunks are decoded for the codec chains the standard library can do (``bytes``/``transpose``/``gzip``/``crc32c``). Anything else routes through the same :func:`require_codec` refusal as v2 does. ``.zgroup`` / ``.zarray`` / ``zarr.json`` and the ``zarr_format`` field are read rather than assumed, and an unsupported ``zarr_format`` is refused by number.
records.context: **0.4 is implemented properly** — it is what essentially all real data is in, and it is zarr-format 2. 0.5 (zarr-format 3, metadata under an ``ome`` structured-data name in ``zarr.json``) is *tolerated*: its metadata is parsed in full, and its chunks are decoded for the codec chains the standard library can do (``bytes``/``transpose``/``gzip``/``crc32c``). Anything else routes through the same :func:`require_codec` refusal as v2 does. ``.zgroup`` / ``.zarray`` / ``zarr.json`` and the ``zarr_format`` field are read rather than assumed, and an unsupported ``zarr_format`` is refused by number.
records.translation: **0.4 är korrekt implementerat** — det är formatet för i stort sett alla verkliga data och använder zarr-format 2. 0.5 (zarr-format 3, med metadata lagrade under nyckeln ``ome`` i ``zarr.json``) *tolereras*: dess metadata tolkas fullständigt och dess block avkodas för de kodekkedjor som standardbiblioteket kan hantera (``bytes``/``transpose``/``gzip``/``crc32c``). Allt annat går genom samma vägran i :func:`require_codec` som v2. ``.zgroup`` / ``.zarray`` / ``zarr.json`` och fältet ``zarr_format`` läses i stället för att antas, och ett ``zarr_format`` som inte stöds avvisas med sitt nummer.

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.project_browser#5
records.source: **The scan never blocks the window.** Walking a plate folder is tens of thousands of ``stat`` calls, and doing it on the GUI thread is a frozen application for however long the filesystem takes. Everything goes through :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`, whose completion handlers here are **bound methods** — read that module's docstring for what a closure connected to ``thread.finished`` costs. The background activity spinner follows the run registry on its own, so nothing here has to drive it.
records.context: **The scan never blocks the window.** Walking a plate folder is tens of thousands of ``stat`` calls, and doing it on the main GUI execution path is a frozen application for however long the filesystem takes. Everything goes through :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`, whose completion handlers here are **bound methods** — read that module's docstring for what a closure connected to ``thread.finished`` costs. The background activity spinner follows the processing session registry on its own, so nothing here has to drive it.
records.translation: **Skanningen blockerar aldrig fönstret.** Att gå igenom en plattmapp är tiotusentals ``stat``-anrop, och att göra det på den huvudsakliga GUI-körningsvägen är en frusen applikation så länge filsystemet tar. Allt går genom :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`, vars slutförande hanterare här är **bundna metoder** — läs den modulen docstring för vad en stängning ansluten till ``thread.finished`` kostar. Bakgrundsaktiviteten spinner följer behandlingssessionsregistret på egen hand, så inget här behöver driva det.

records.source: :mod:`spacr.qt.imagery` has always run every photographic master through :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.solve_dim` against :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.exposure_target` — the brightest a bare window background may be before white text on it drops under WCAG AA. The generated sky never went through it, and it showed: measured at 1440x900, the brightest text-line-sized region of the ``galaxy`` sky was 0.4879 against a 0.0586 limit (8.3x over), ``sun`` 0.8201 (14.0x) and ``stars`` 0.5041 (8.6x). Bare white text over that measured 1.20-1.96:1 where 4.5:1 is required — the "AI" toggle in the title bar sat on the sun's halo. :func:`render` now solves it, and :func:`legibility` reports the same measured dict :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.legibility` returns for a photograph.

The generated sky never went through it, and it showed: measured at 1440x900, the brightest text-line-sized region of the ``galaxy`` sky was 0.4879 against a 0.0586 limit (8.3x over), ``sun`` 0.8201 (14.0x) and ``stars`` 0.5041 (8.6x). Bare white text over that measured 1.20-1.96:1 where 4.5:1 is required — the "AI" toggle in the title bar sat on the sun's halo. :func:`render` now solves it, and :func:`legibility` reports the same measured key-value mapping :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.legibility` returns for a photograph.
records.translation: :mod:`spacr.qt.imagery` har alltid kört varje fotografiskt original genom :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.solve_dim` mot :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.exposure_target` — den högsta ljusstyrkan en bar fönsterbakgrund får ha innan vit text understiger WCAG AA. Den genererade himlen gick aldrig genom detta, vilket syntes: vid 1440x900 mättes den ljusaste regionen i textradhöjd i himlen ``galaxy`` till 0.4879 mot gränsen 0.0586 (8.3x över), ``sun`` till 0.8201 (14.0x) och ``stars`` till 0.5041 (8.6x). Bar vit text över dessa områden gav 1.20-1.96:1 där 4.5:1 krävs — reglaget "AI" i titelraden låg på solens halo. :func:`render` löser nu detta, och :func:`legibility` rapporterar samma uppmätta nyckel-värde-mappning som :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.legibility` returnerar för ett fotografi.

records.label: spacr.qt.verbose_logger#2
records.source: The handler is a lazy module-level singleton so multiple :func:`apply_verbose_logging` calls (e.g. every time the Preferences dialog is saved) don't stack up handlers or leak references. Turning verbose off leaves the handler attached but silent — cheaper than tearing it down and rebuilding it, and safer for cases where a log record fires mid-toggle.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.ambient#5
records.source: ``aurora`` Three overlapping curtains of vertical rays, folding along their own length. The folds are travelling waves — several superposed frequencies running lengthwise along the arc — with brightness surges on a separate schedule, a sharp lower edge, a diffuse top, and the real thing's vertical colour order: green through the body, red high up, a violet fringe underneath. ``ripple`` Concentric rings expanding out of three fixed sources and fading as they grow, like rain on water. Soft-edged, so it never reads as line work. ``drift`` A slow starfield in three parallax layers: small, dim, slow ones behind; bigger, brighter, faster ones in front. The one crisp theme. It travels up, down, or every which way — see :data:`DRIFT_DIRECTIONS`. ``bokeh`` Out-of-focus points of light, the way a fluorescence field looks off the focal plane: an aperture image is a *disc with a bright rim*, not a Gaussian smudge, and the ones further out of focus are larger and flatter. ``cells`` Cells drifting through the field, turning as they go — a soft body, a slightly brighter membrane where the edge is seen nearly edge-on, and a distinctly brighter nucleus set off centre.
records.context: ``aurora`` Three overlapping curtains of vertical rays, folding along their own length. The folds are travelling waves — several superposed frequencies running lengthwise along the arc — with brightness surges on a separate schedule, a sharp lower edge, a diffuse top, and the real thing's vertical colour order: green through the body, red high up, a violet fringe underneath. ``ripple`` Concentric rings expanding out of three fixed sources and fading as they grow, like rain on water. Soft-edged, so it never reads as line work. ``drift`` A slow starfield in three parallax layers: small, dim, slow ones behind; bigger, brighter, faster ones in front. The one crisp theme. It travels up, down, or every which way — see :data:`DRIFT_DIRECTIONS`. ``bokeh`` Out-of-focus points of light, the way a fluorescence field looks off the focal image layer: an aperture image is a *disc with a bright rim*, not a Gaussian smudge, and the ones further out of focus are larger and flatter. ``cells`` Cells drifting through the field, turning as they go — a soft body, a slightly brighter membrane where the edge is seen nearly edge-on, and a distinctly brighter nucleus set off centre.
records.translation: ``aurora`` Tre överlappande gardiner av lodräta strålar som veckas längs sin egen längd. Vecken är vandrande vågor — flera överlagrade frekvenser längs bågen — med ljusstyrkeökningar enligt ett separat schema, en skarp nedre kant, en diffus ovansida och norrskenets verkliga lodräta färgordning: grönt genom kroppen, rött högt upp och en violett frans undertill. ``ripple`` Koncentriska ringar som växer från tre fasta källor och bleknar medan de växer, som regn på vatten. Kanterna är mjuka så att de aldrig ser ut som linjeteckningar. ``drift`` Ett långsamt stjärnfält i tre parallaxlager: små, svaga och långsamma stjärnor bakom; större, ljusare och snabbare framför. Det enda skarpa temat. Det rör sig uppåt, nedåt eller åt alla håll — se :data:`DRIFT_DIRECTIONS`. ``bokeh`` Oskärpepunkter av ljus, så som ett fluorescensfält ser ut utanför fokusplanet: en bländarbild är en *skiva med ljus kant*, inte en Gaussisk fläck, och punkter längre ur fokus är större och plattare. ``cells`` Celler driver genom fältet och vrider sig på vägen — en mjuk kropp, ett något ljusare membran där kanten ses nästan från sidan och en tydligt ljusare kärna placerad utanför mitten.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.column_picker#7
records.source: **Read-only.** Opening the picker reads column names and nothing else. The connection is ``file:…?mode=ro`` plus ``PRAGMA query_only = ON`` — the same pair :mod:`spacr.qt.screens.db_browser` and :mod:`spacr.agreement` use — so SQLite itself refuses a write. The dialog never creates a column: it returns a *name*, and the write path that owns creation (``annotate_engine.ensure_annotation_column``, which does it lazily with ``ALTER TABLE``) stays where it is.
